title: Court Marriage in Bangladesh: Legal Process, Real Costs & Document Checklist
metaTitle: Court Marriage in Bangladesh: Procedure & Costs | Adv. Shah Alam
metaDescription: Definitivelegal guide to court marriage in Bangladesh. Distinguish Notary public affidavits from authorized Kazi registration. Official fee schedule & document rules.
heroIntro: In Bangladesh, societal resistance or inter-religious backgrounds often compel consenting adults to solemnize their union through what is popularly known as a 'Court Marriage'. However, falling prey to unauthorized street notaries and bogus deed writers who sell meaningless BDT 500 stamp affidavits leads to severe legal trauma. A notary public affidavit does not constitute a valid marriage under Bangladesh family laws; without formal registration before an authorized Muslim Marriage Registrar (Kazi) or Special Marriage Registrar, the union remains invalid, jeopardizing the wife's statutory dower (Mahr), alimony, and inheritance rights. What is the authorized legal procedure, what are the official gazetted fees in 2026, and how can couples protect themselves from retaliatory abduction FIRs? Below is a practical guide by Supreme Court practitioner Advocate Md. Shah Alam. Call directly at +880 1712-655546.

quickAnswer.heading: ⚡ Quick Legal Answer: Court Marriage in Bangladesh
points: A standalone Notary Public Affidavit does not create a valid marriage under Bangladesh law.
The legal procedure requires both an Affidavit of Free Will and formal registration in the statutory register of an authorized Kazi or Special Marriage Registrar.
Statutory age qualifications: Groom must be 21+ years old and Bride must be 18+ years old under the Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017.
Government Kazi fee is fixed at BDT 14 per BDT 1,000 up to the first BDT 4,00,000 of Mahr, and BDT 100 per additional BDT 1,00,000.
The free-will affidavit serves as vital legal protection to immediately quash false abduction complaints (Nari O Shishu Act Sec 7/8) filed by disgruntled families.

sections.heading: 1. The Legal Reality of Court Marriage in Bangladesh
sections.content:
Strictly speaking, the phrase 'Court Marriage' does not exist as a statutory concept in Bangladesh legislation. Instead, it refers to a two-step legal procedure combining:

  1. A formal Affidavit of Declaration and Mutual Consent sworn before a 1st Class Judicial Magistrate or Notary Public; and
  2. Solemnization and registration under personal status laws (such as the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Act 1974 or the Special Marriage Act 1872).

Both elements are necessary to achieve complete legal security and religious validity.

sections.heading: 2. Notary Affidavit vs Kazi Registration: The Common Fatal Mistake
sections.content:
A widespread legal pitfall in Bangladesh is the belief that an affidavit stamped by a Notary Public constitutes a complete marriage. In landmark judgments, the High Court Division has repeatedly affirmed that a notary public holds no power to solemnize a marriage.

The affidavit serves merely as evidentiary proof of the parties' majority, mental sanity, and uncoerced consent. The substantive validity of the marriage springs solely from the statutory registration recorded in the official marriage register (Nikahnama).

sections.heading: 3. Mandatory Eligibility Criteria and Required Documents
sections.content:
Before initiating the court marriage process, couples must ensure the following documentation is intact:

  • Proof of Majority: National ID Cards (Smart NID) or digital online birth certificates. The groom must be at least 21 years old and the bride at least 18 years old under the Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017.
  • Passport Photographs: 3 to 4 passport-size photographs of both parties.
  • Adult Witnesses: Two adult male witnesses (or one male and two females) holding valid National IDs.

sections.heading: 4. Official Government Fees and Realistic Court Expenses in 2026
sections.content:
Statutory government fees are prescribed by the Ministry of Law and Judicial Affairs:

  • Non-Judicial Stamp Paper: BDT 300 government stamp for the affidavit.
  • Notary Public Attestation: Standard fee between BDT 500 and BDT 1,000.
  • Government Kazi Registry Fee: BDT 14 per thousand up to the first BDT 4,00,000 of Mahr (maximum BDT 5,600). For Mahr amounts above BDT 4,00,000, the fee is BDT 100 per additional BDT 1,00,000.
  • Certified Nikahnama Extract: BDT 100 to BDT 300 for obtaining official certified copies.

sections.heading: 5. Step-by-Step Procedure for Completing Court Marriage
sections.content:
The lawful execution follows three consecutive stages:

  1. Drafting the Affidavit: A lawyer drafts the declaration of marriage on non-judicial stamp paper affirming free consent and sound mental state.
  2. Execution before Magistrate / Notary: Both parties appear in person, verify identity through biometric NID checks, and swear the oath.
  3. Nikah Registry Execution: The couple proceeds to an authorized Muslim Marriage Registrar, completes the 25-column Nikahnama, ensures Column 18 (delegated divorce rights) is executed, and receives the marriage certificate.

sections.heading: 6. Interfaith Unions under the Special Marriage Act 1872
sections.content:
When bride and groom belong to different religious faiths (such as Hindu-Muslim or Muslim-Christian) and neither wishes to renounce their religion or undergo conversion, they can marry under the Special Marriage Act, 1872.

This requires a 14-day statutory notice period before the Special Marriage Registrar. The marriage creates full civil legality, and children born of such unions have full inheritance rights under civil property statutes.

sections.heading: 7. Defending Against False Abduction and Kidnapping Charges
sections.content:
A common hazard following court marriage is that aggrieved relatives file a First Information Report (FIR) alleging abduction under Sections 7 or 8 of the Prevention of Women and Children Repression Act 2000 (Nari O Shishu Nirjaton Daman Ain).

Protective Legal Strategy:

  • Promptly record a General Diary (GD) enclosing certified copies of the Nikahnama and Notary Affidavit at the local police station.
  • If an FIR is initiated, the bride should appear voluntarily before the Cognizance Magistrate under Section 22 / 164 CrPC to record her voluntary statement confirming her lawful marriage and majority.

faqs.question: Can a court marriage take place without parental consent in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. If both parties have attained legal adulthood (male 21, female 18), they possess the absolute constitutional right to marry without parental permission.

faqs.question: How long does a court marriage take in Dhaka?
faqs.answer: If documents and adult witnesses are ready, the entire process—including affidavit execution and Nikah registration—is typically completed within 2 to 4 hours.

faqs.question: Is an interfaith marriage valid without religious conversion in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the Special Marriage Act 1872, individuals of different faiths can lawfully marry without religious conversion.
